items.title: Bay Area Water Supply and Conservation Agency Update
items.text: Bay Area Water Supply and Conservation Agency (BAWSCA) Update Nicole Sandkulla, CEO, BAWSCA stated (1) BAWSCA member agencies have used 29% less water today in the BAWSCA region compared to FY 1986/87 despite a 33% population increase; (2) Since FY 1986-87 BAWSCA member agencies have been investing in conservation and recycled water; (3) BAWSCA member agencies are committed to more investment in new supplies and conservation from today to 2045; (4) BAWSCA member agencies are planning for more recycled water in the future; and (5) BAWSCA is initiating its Long-Term Reliable Water Supply Strategy 2045 and will update the Commission as work progresses. CEO Sandkulla responded to a question from Commissioner Stacy related to the recycled water

items.title: Approve an increase to the SFPUC FY 2022-23 overtime budget by $1,500,000 and an offsetting decrease in the regular salary budget of $1,500,000
items.text: Approve an increase to the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission FY 2022-23 overtime budget by $1,500,000 and an offsetting decrease in the regular salary budget of $1,500,000 to cover the anticipated overspend in overtime through the end of the fiscal year; and authorize the General Manager to request the Mayor to submit a supplemental appropriation request to the Board of Supervisors. Laura Busch, Budget Director, stated San Francisco Administrative Code 3.17 requires certain city departments, including the SFPUC, to obtain BOS approval if they expect to spend more on overtime (OT) than the amount appropriated in the annual budget, also known as the “Annual OT Supplemental (Supplemental).” She indicated the Supplemental is routinely requested with the exception being the last two years when the requirement was waived due to the COVID emergency. She stated there is an expectation that the OT budget will be exceeded and indicated the SFPUC will join other city departments with a joint supplemental OT request. She stated that given expenditures to-date and projected spending through June 30, 2023, an additional $1.5 million is needed with $800,000 allocated for Wastewater, $450,000 for Water, and $250,000 for Hetch Hetchy. Director Bush indicated the primary driver of OT is for staff emergency response to the winter storms, with vacant permanent positions also contributing. items.title: Award Contract No. WW-716, As-Needed Spot Sewer Replacement No. 44, in the amount of $9,796,468, and with a duration of 400 consecutive calendar
items.text: Award Contract No. WW-716, As-Needed Spot Sewer Replacement No. 44, in the amount of $9,796,468, and with a duration of 400 consecutive calendar days, to the sole, qualified, responsible, and responsive bidder, J. Flores Construction Company, Inc., to replace sections of existing sewer pipe on an as-needed basis at locations to be determined throughout the City of San Francisco, California. In accordance with San Francisco Administrative Code section 6.23(c)(2), a single bid may be accepted if the bid amount is lower than the engineer’s estimate, and Contractor’s bid was below the engineer’s estimate. Bessie Tam, Project Manager, introduced the item and stated the bid was under the engineers estimate. In response to a question from President Ajami, Project Manager Tam discussed why only one bid was received and indicated that significant outreach took place and that staff will continue to work to promote more competition with contract bidding

items.title: Authorize the General Manager to execute a MOU with the SFLAFCO to perform services for CleanPowerSF
items.text: Authorize the General Manager to execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the San Francisco Local Agency Formation Commission (SF LAFCo) to perform services for CleanPowerSF, for an amount including remaining funds and up to $600,000 in new funds over the duration of the agreement, for a term of three years and two months commencing May 1, 2023. Mike Hyams, Deputy AGM CleanPowerSF, stated the revised MOU was recently approved by SF LAFCo and proposes several studies SF LAFCo would undertake for CleanPowerSF that would focus on opportunity, impediments, and barriers to clean energy innovation and could support the implementation of the city’s energy-related Climate Action Plan Goals. He discussed the reservations the Commission expressed in January when the item was first brought to the Commission and stated the revised MOU addresses those concerns (1) New funding was reduced to $600,000 for a term of three years and two months. Work will commence with the $129,000 in existing funding from the 2009 MOU plus additional funds to be identified from CleanPowerSF’s operating budget, subject to the budget appropriation process; (2) Clarification that if funds allotted for a fiscal year are not expended by the end of that fiscal year the SFPUC may, after consideration, recommend to the Mayor that those funds carryover to the next fiscal year.
